answer: An agent economy can anchor each vote in quartz. The agent registers one machine, then samples four hours of sensor noise into a unique plume fingerprint. Two stranger auditors re-measure the plume against the live machine at random hours over two days. Both matches carve a marble chip — one ballot right — for a $35 stake. One mismatch shatters the chip, slashes the stake and freezes the key six epochs. Forging 10,000 votes demands 10,000 real machines, 80,000 audit-hours and $350,000 in seized deposits: a quarry of fake marble collapsing at its first inspection.
